title: Sustained alpha-dominated magnetic-confinement operation
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Sustain a magnetically confined plasma in which fusion alpha particles supply most heating while density, impurities, pressure, and current remain controlled.
status: Decades of externally heated experiments support extrapolation, but the cited gain surveys distinguish these from sustained reactor-like burning operation.
why: External heating can conceal instabilities and power-balance problems that appear when the plasma heats itself.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2022), *Progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criterion*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990; arXiv:2105.10954.

title: Alpha-particle redistribution under overlapping modes
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Predict alpha redistribution and wall losses when several energetic-particle modes overlap, including nonlinear saturation and evolving background profiles.
status: Single-mode theory and extensive experiments exist; the burning-plasma, multimode extrapolation remains a central uncertainty.
why: Alpha losses simultaneously reduce heating and concentrate damaging power on walls.
key_works: Chen and Zonca (2016), *Physics of Alfvén waves and energetic particles in burning plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.88.015008.

title: Reactor-geometry Dimits-shift prediction
open: Predict the nonlinear turbulence threshold above the linear instability threshold in realistic electromagnetic, multispecies, shaped plasmas.
status: Reduced-model explanations and three-dimensional studies exist; a quantitatively reliable reactor-geometry theory remains incomplete.
why: The difference between linear and nonlinear thresholds strongly affects predicted confinement.
key_works: Ivanov et al. (2020), *Zonally dominated dynamics and Dimits threshold in curvature-driven ITG turbulence*, DOI: 10.1017/S0022377820000938; arXiv:2004.04047.

title: Predictive ion–electron turbulence coupling
open: Quantify when electron-scale turbulence changes ion-scale transport, and vice versa, across reactor-relevant gradients, magnetic geometry, and beta.
status: Multiscale simulations demonstrated enhanced transport from cross-scale coupling by 2014–2016; economical predictive coverage remains limited.
why: Simulating either scale alone can give the wrong heat loss.
key_works: Howard et al. (2016), *Multi-scale gyrokinetic simulations: Comparison with experiment and implications for predicting turbulence and transport*, *Physics of Plasmas* 23, 056109.

title: Hydrogen-isotope confinement effect
open: Explain and predict how confinement changes between hydrogen, deuterium, tritium, and mixtures after controlling for heating, profiles, walls, and operating regime.
status: The effect has decades of experimental history; the 2023 review documents multiple mechanisms and unresolved mixture physics.
why: Deuterium experiments must reliably predict deuterium–tritium performance.
key_works: Ida (2023), *Isotope effect of transport and key physics in the isotope mixture plasmas*, DOI: 10.1007/s41614-023-00126-3.

title: Fuel-density peaking without impurity accumulation
open: Identify controllable regimes that increase central fuel density without producing unacceptable inward transport of high-charge impurities.
status: Neoclassical and turbulent impurity models exist, but their combined reactor operating window is not established.
why: Density peaking can increase fusion power, whereas impurity peaking can terminate the discharge.
key_works: Donnel et al. (2018), *Self-consistent gyrokinetic modeling of neoclassical and turbulent impurity transport*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/aa6ebb.

title: Neoclassical-tearing-mode seed threshold
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict the minimum perturbation that seeds a damaging neoclassical tearing mode under evolving reactor pressure and current profiles.
status: The 2006 review established the major framework; seed formation and extrapolation remain distinct from linear stability.
why: Avoiding a seed may require far less control power than suppressing a mature island.
key_works: La Haye (2006), *Neoclassical tearing modes and their control*, DOI: 10.1063/1.2180747.

title: Out-of-distribution disruption prediction
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict disruptions on new machines and unfamiliar operating regimes with calibrated warning times, missed-event rates, and false-alarm costs.
status: Deep learning demonstrated cross-device progress in 2019; reliable extrapolation to reactor conditions remains unresolved.
why: A predictor that fails on the first unfamiliar dangerous event is not a protection system.
key_works: Kates-Harbeck, Svyatkovskiy, and Tang (2019), *Predicting disruptive instabilities in controlled fusion plasmas through deep learning*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-019-1116-4.

title: Shattered-pellet assimilation
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict and control how injected fragments ablate, penetrate, mix, and radiate during a disruption, including asymmetric deposition.
status: Shattered-pellet injection is a developed mitigation approach; reactor-scale assimilation remains an active validation need.
why: Injecting material is useful only if it reaches and cools the plasma as intended.
key_works: Lehnen et al. (2015), *Disruptions in ITER and strategies for their control and mitigation*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2014.10.075.

title: Runaway seed prediction during thermal quench
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict the runaway seed from hot-tail, Dreicer, radioactive, and externally driven sources during realistic rapid cooling.
status: The 2019 runaway review synthesizes these mechanisms; their combined reactor prediction remains uncertain.
why: A small seed can become a destructive relativistic-electron population.
key_works: Breizman et al. (2019), *Physics of runaway electrons in tokamaks*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ab1822.

title: Runaway-free startup
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Establish startup waveforms and fueling strategies that avoid runaway formation despite uncertain prefill, impurities, and wall conditions.
status: Startup runaway generation was modeled explicitly in 2022; avoiding it across realistic operational variability remains open.
why: Dangerous electron populations can arise before normal confinement is established.
key_works: Hoppe et al. (2022), *Runaway electron generation during tokamak start-up*, DOI: 10.1017/S002237782200054X; arXiv:2203.09900.

title: Advanced-divertor reactor scaling
open: Establish whether Super-X, snowflake, X-point-target, and related geometries retain their advantages under reactor constraints on coils, shielding, pumping, and control.
status: Advanced geometries have experimental and modeling support; full plant integration remains unresolved.
why: Geometric heat spreading may relax the most severe material requirements.
key_works: Leonard (2018), *Plasma detachment in divertor tokamaks*; NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991.

title: Exact force-free toroidal equilibria with nested surfaces
open: Determine whether exact analytic nonaxisymmetric force-free toroidal fields can possess the desired nested-surface structure.
status: Explicitly unresolved in the September 2026 analytic-equilibrium paper; it is distinct from the newly constructed finite-pressure families.
why: It connects stellarator geometry to current-carrying low-pressure equilibria.
key_works: Landreman (2026), *Analytic toroidal 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows with invariant surfaces*, arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Piecewise-omnigenous collisional transport
open: Determine the collisional and finite-orbit-width transport generated at transitions between approximately omnigenous regions.
status: Generalized omnigenity and newer optimization methods enlarge the design space; realistic transport across their boundaries needs validation.
why: Good collisionless orbits need not imply acceptable thermal transport.
key_works: *Magnetic Fields with General Omnigenity* (2024 version), arXiv:2305.08026; *Optimizing omnigenity like quasisymmetry for stellarators* (2025), arXiv:2502.09350.

title: Solenoid-free spherical-tokamak startup
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Produce a reactor-relevant spherical-tokamak current and closed-flux configuration without a conventional central solenoid.
status: Alternative startup methods exist, but the complete reactor trajectory remains a development problem.
why: The narrow center column leaves little space for startup hardware and shielding.
key_works: Menard et al. (2016), *Fusion nuclear science facilities and pilot plants based on the spherical tokamak*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/56/10/106023.

title: Simultaneous mirror microstability and MHD stability
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Find mirror distributions that suppress loss-cone and other kinetic instabilities while also satisfying macroscopic interchange stability.
status: Stabilization mechanisms exist individually; a reactor-quality combined window remains unresolved.
why: Fixing one instability can worsen another or increase end losses.
key_works: Ivanov and Prikhodko (2013), *Gas-dynamic trap: an overview of the concept and experimental results*.

title: Positive FRC beam-sustainment balance
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Demonstrate that neutral-beam-maintained FRC fusion output can exceed the complete power required to sustain the configuration.
status: Beam-generated FRCs were reported in 2025; formation itself is therefore not the open problem.
why: Strong beam support can improve confinement while masking an unfavorable power balance.
key_works: Roche et al. (2025), *Generation of field-reversed configurations via neutral beam injection*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-58849-5.

title: Kinetic stabilization of reactor-scale FRCs
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Predict whether favorable finite-orbit and energetic-ion stabilization persists as FRC size, collisionality, and fusion-product populations change.
status: High-performance beam-supported FRC states exist; reactor-scale stability remains an extrapolation.
why: Stabilization observed in one kinetic regime may not survive scaling.
key_works: Steinhauer (2011), *Review of field-reversed configurations*; Roche et al. (2025), DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-58849-5.

title: Sheared-flow Z-pinch scaling to gain
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Demonstrate that shear-flow stabilization survives at the density, temperature, current, and duration required for fusion gain.
status: Sustained neutron production and thermonuclear-origin measurements exist; these do not establish reactor gain.
why: It tests a potentially simple, magnet-light confinement architecture.
key_works: Shumlak (2020), *Z-pinch fusion*, *Journal of Applied Physics* 127, 200901; Mitrani et al. (2021), DOI: 10.1063/5.0066257.

title: Plasma-jet liner assembly
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Merge many plasma jets into a sufficiently uniform, low-entropy imploding liner with acceptable mass, momentum, and timing variation.
status: Plasma-liner concepts have an established research history; high-gain target compression remains unresolved.
why: A standoff driver could protect hardware from the fusion chamber.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2022), *Progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criterion*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990.

title: Direct-drive ignition
open: Demonstrate actual ignition and useful target gain using direct laser drive, rather than hydrodynamically scaled equivalence.
status: A hydrodynamically equivalent burning-plasma demonstration was published in 2024; that result is not direct-drive ignition itself.
why: Direct drive could offer different efficiency and target-manufacturing tradeoffs.
key_works: Gopalaswamy et al. (2024), *Demonstration of a hydrodynamically equivalent burning plasma in direct-drive inertial confinement fusion*, DOI: 10.1038/s41567-023-02361-4.

title: Predictive cross-beam energy transfer
open: Predict and control cross-beam energy transfer in evolving, multidimensional target plasmas over the full pulse.
status: Wavelength detuning demonstrated mitigation in 2018; complete predictive control across target designs remains open.
why: Energy redistribution changes implosion symmetry and useful coupling.
key_works: Marozas et al. (2018), *First observation of cross-beam energy transfer mitigation for direct-drive inertial confinement fusion implosions using wavelength detuning at the national ignition facility*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.085001.

title: Repeatedly demountable HTS joints
open: Repeatedly disconnect and reconnect reactor magnet joints while preserving electrical, mechanical, and vacuum performance.
status: Demountable magnets are a prominent compact-reactor design feature; lifecycle qualification remains unresolved.
why: Demountability could transform maintenance access, but only if joints remain reliable.
key_works: Sorbom et al. (2015), *ARC: A compact, high-field, fusion nuclear science facility and demonstration power plant with demountable magnets*, DOI: 10.1016/j.fusengdes.2015.07.008; Hartwig et al. (2024).

title: Rapid outer-cycle tritium recovery
open: Recover bred tritium from blanket fluids or solids quickly enough to satisfy dynamic fuel-self-sufficiency requirements.
status: ARC- and STEP-class models published in 2023 show the importance of coupled inventories and processing times.
why: A favorable long-run breeding ratio can coexist with short-run fuel starvation.
key_works: Meschini et al. (2023), *Modeling and analysis of the tritium fuel cycle for ARC- and STEP-class D-T fusion power plants*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/acf3fc.

title: Rapid remote divertor replacement
open: Demonstrate complete removal, replacement, reconnection, inspection, and recommissioning of representative activated divertor modules.
status: DEMO studies estimate substantial maintenance durations; these are planning estimates, not demonstrated reactor turnaround records.
why: Divertor replacement frequency may dominate capacity factor.
key_works: Crofts and Harman (2014), *Maintenance Duration Estimate for a DEMO Fusion Power Plant*, DOI: 10.1016/j.fusengdes.2014.01.038.

title: Evidence-based fusion availability models
open: Replace largely assumed component failure and repair rates with traceable measurements, dependence models, and validated plant-level availability predictions.
status: Maintenance-duration studies and pilot-plant analyses exist; operating-fleet reliability data do not yet underpin them.
why: Availability assumptions can dominate electricity-cost estimates.
key_works: Crofts and Harman (2014), arXiv:1412.4008; NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*.

title: Affordable full nonlinear Coulomb collisions
open: Implement the full nonlinear gyrokinetic Coulomb operator at production scale without replacing important velocity-space structure by uncontrolled model collisions.
status: The nonlinear operator has already been derived; the open problem is computationally affordable use in demanding electromagnetic, multispecies simulations.
why: Collision-model choices can influence transport thresholds, impurity behavior, and irreversible heating.
key_works: Jorge, Frei, and Ricci (2019), *Nonlinear Gyrokinetic Coulomb Collision Operator*, arXiv:1906.03252.

title: Reactive collisions with changing charge states
open: Couple gyrokinetic Coulomb collisions to ionization, recombination, and charge exchange while preserving the appropriate particle, momentum, and total-energy balances across changing species populations.
status: A nonlinear Coulomb operator alone does not supply the reactive collision system required for partially ionized edge plasmas.
why: Incorrect source coupling can create artificial energy or impurity transport near the plasma boundary.
key_works: Jorge, Frei, and Ricci (2019), *Nonlinear Gyrokinetic Coulomb Collision Operator*, arXiv:1906.03252; Osborne et al. (2024–2025), arXiv:2410.14403.

title: Conservation and positivity under adaptive remeshing
open: Preserve positivity, conservation, and the discrete entropy law when collision calculations are combined with velocity-grid adaptation, spatial remeshing, and transfers between kinetic representations.
status: Discretizations satisfying these properties already exist for the nonlinear Landau operator. The unresolved extension is maintaining them through the additional operations used by practical adaptive simulations.
why: Remeshing should not introduce negative populations or erase physically important tails.
key_works: Hirvijoki, Burby, and Kraus (2018), *Energy-, momentum-, density-, and positivity-preserving spatio-temporal discretizations for the nonlinear Landau collision operator with exact H-theorems*, arXiv:1804.08546.

title: Three-dimensional gyrokinetic dissipation anomaly
open: Establish whether driven electromagnetic gyrokinetic turbulence retains finite irreversible entropy production as physical collisionality tends to zero, and specify the required regularity and forcing assumptions.
status: Entropy-cascade theory and reduced gyrokinetic studies provide a foundation; the full three-dimensional electromagnetic statement is stronger.
why: It would clarify how nearly collisionless plasma converts turbulent energy into heat.
key_works: Tatsuno et al. (2008 preprint), *Nonlinear phase mixing and phase-space cascade of entropy in gyrokinetic plasma turbulence*, arXiv:0811.2538.

title: Turbulent lifetime distributions near threshold
open: Determine whether near-threshold plasma turbulence decays, persists indefinitely, or exhibits system-size-dependent metastability, and measure the corresponding lifetime distributions.
status: MAST-oriented studies connect subcritical simulations to measurements; distinguishing long transients from genuinely sustained states remains essential.
why: A discharge lasting less than a turbulent lifetime can misidentify the underlying stability boundary.
key_works: van Wyk et al. (2017), *Ion-scale turbulence in MAST: anomalous transport, subcritical transitions, and comparison to BES measurements*, arXiv:1704.02830.

title: Staircase survival under reactor scaling
open: Determine whether transport staircases survive decreasing normalized gyroradius, evolving profiles, electromagnetic turbulence, and realistic sources, rather than being finite-domain structures.
status: Global simulations established staircase phenomenology; reactor-scale persistence is a separate extrapolation problem.
why: A confinement mechanism that disappears with size cannot justify reactor design assumptions.
key_works: Dif-Pradalier et al. (2017), *The E×B staircase of magnetised plasmas*.

title: Correct isotope scaling of molecular charge exchange
open: Replace simple hydrogen-to-deuterium/tritium mass rescaling with validated, state-resolved molecular charge-exchange rates for the isotopic mixtures used in reactors.
status: A 2023 SOLPS-ITER investigation showed that default rescaling could underestimate molecular-ion production and materially change predicted detachment behavior.
why: Incorrect rates can produce the wrong recombination, radiation, and target-current predictions.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigating the impact of the molecular charge-exchange rate on detached SOLPS-ITER simulations*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/acd394; arXiv:2301.11298.

title: Negative-ion contribution to molecular-assisted recombination
open: Separate and quantify recombination mediated by negative hydrogen isotopes from pathways involving positive molecular ions under strongly detached conditions.
status: MAST-U studies identify molecular channels and possible negative-ion contributions; their relative importance requires stronger experimental discrimination.
why: Different pathways respond differently to isotope composition, vibrational excitation, and electron temperature.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigations of atomic & molecular processes of NBI-heated discharges in the MAST Upgrade Super-X divertor with implications for reactors*, arXiv:2311.08580.

title: Molecular-assisted dissociation power accounting
open: Close the power balance for molecular-assisted dissociation, including fragment kinetic energy, subsequent ionization, radiation, and energy ultimately deposited on surfaces.
status: MAST-U analyses infer consequential dissociation-related power sinks; a reaction’s local energy removal is not necessarily its net plant-facing exhaust benefit.
why: Misallocated chemical energy can create apparent unexplained divertor power.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigations of atomic & molecular processes of NBI-heated discharges in the MAST Upgrade Super-X divertor with implications for reactors*, arXiv:2311.08580.

title: Sub-electronvolt ion–molecule elastic collisions
open: Validate momentum and energy-transfer operators for ion–molecule elastic collisions in the very cold regions of detached divertors.
status: Dedicated SOLPS-ITER predictions published in 2023 examine these collisions in strongly detached MAST-U conditions; direct discriminating validation remains needed.
why: Processes negligible in hotter plasma can control pressure balance below approximately one electronvolt.
key_works: Myatra et al. (2023), *SOLPS-ITER predictive simulations of the impact of ion-molecule elastic collisions on strongly detached MAST-U Super-X divertor conditions*, *Nuclear Fusion* 63, 076030.

title: Sheath structure below the critical grazing angle
open: Determine the physically selected sheath configuration below the angle at which monotonic solutions cease to exist, allowing kinetic electrons and finite Debye length.
status: A 2025 study characterizes monotonic grazing-incidence sheaths and their critical-angle boundary; the boundary is not a complete description of the state below it.
why: Reactor divertors deliberately use shallow incidence to spread heat.
key_works: Geraldini et al. (2025), *Characteristics of monotonic sheaths near a wall with grazing magnetic incidence*, arXiv:2508.09067.

title: Secondary-emission sheath transitions on reactor surfaces
open: Establish when irradiated, contaminated, or evolving plasma-facing surfaces enter emission-dominated sheath states and determine their consequences for electron heat flux.
status: The absence of a conventional Debye sheath under strong secondary emission was demonstrated theoretically in 2012; reactor-surface transition maps remain a separate problem.
why: Surface emission can invalidate standard wall-potential and heat-transmission assumptions.
key_works: Campanell, Khrabrov, and Kaganovich (2012), *Absence of Debye Sheaths due to Secondary Electron Emission*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.255001.

title: Consequences of the unfavorable maximum-J minority
open: Determine whether the small population of particles violating maximum-J behavior in optimized vacuum quasi-isodynamic fields can drive consequential instabilities or losses.
status: A published construction gives favorable behavior for 99.6% of trapped particles while identifying an unavoidable unfavorable shallowly trapped population.
why: A small phase-space fraction can matter disproportionately if it resonates strongly.
key_works: Rodríguez, Helander, and Goodman (2023 preprint), *The maximum-J property in quasi-isodynamic stellarators*, arXiv:2311.14439.

title: Uniform treatment of merging neoclassical regimes
open: Extend asymptotic descriptions of merging superbanana-plateau and square-root-collisionality regimes to realistic profiles, multiple species, and departures from near-quasisymmetry.
status: Catto, Tolman, and Parra derived a merged treatment for nearly quasisymmetric stellarators in 2023; the restricted result should not be mistaken for a universal closure.
why: Regime boundaries can occur inside the operating window of an optimized reactor.
key_works: Catto et al. (2023), *Merging of the superbanana plateau and √ν transport regimes in nearly quasisymmetric stellarators*, DOI: 10.1017/S0022377822001301.

title: Full flux-surface electrostatic-potential maps
open: Measure the three-dimensional electrostatic variation on a flux surface accurately enough to discriminate competing impurity-transport models.
status: TJ-II measurements reported substantial potential variations and partial agreement with calculations; local discrepancies remained.
why: Small potential variations relative to bulk temperature can strongly affect high-charge impurities.
key_works: Pedrosa et al. (2015), *Electrostatic potential variations along flux surfaces in stellarators*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/55/5/052001; arXiv:1404.0932.

title: Electric-root transition fronts
open: Predict the position, propagation, and stability of transitions between ambipolar electric-field roots, including finite orbit widths and profile feedback.
status: Neoclassical theory identifies strong radial-electric-field dependence; selecting a spatially evolving root is more demanding than solving a local ambipolarity equation.
why: Root transitions can reorganize confinement and impurity transport.
key_works: Calvo et al. (2017), *The effect of tangential drifts on neoclassical transport in stellarators close to omnigeneity*, arXiv:1610.06016.

title: Nonlinear significance of stellarator zonal-flow oscillations
open: Determine when the observed oscillatory relaxation of radial electric fields materially changes sustained turbulence rather than merely describing a linear relaxation experiment.
status: Oscillatory relaxation was observed experimentally in 2017, and semianalytical frequency calculations exist.
why: A measurable mode is useful for design only if its nonlinear confinement role is understood.
key_works: Alonso et al. (2017), *Observation of Oscillatory Radial Electric Field Relaxation in a Stellarator Plasma*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.185002; Monreal et al. (2017), arXiv:1701.02722.

title: Self-consistent pressure flattening near stellarator islands
open: Determine island pressure profiles and associated currents from coupled transport and equilibrium, rather than prescribing flattening independently.
status: Pressure-driven currents near islands were analyzed in 2016; self-consistent profile selection remains a further coupled problem.
why: Assumed pressure flattening changes both predicted island structure and stability.
key_works: Reiman et al. (2016), *Pressure driven currents near magnetic islands in 3D MHD equilibria*, *Physics of Plasmas* 23, 072502.

title: Dynamically accessible island elimination
open: Establish when boundary adjustments that eliminate islands in equilibrium calculations can actually produce the desired state through finite-resistivity plasma evolution.
status: High-pressure free-boundary equilibrium optimization demonstrated island elimination in 2002; equilibrium existence does not establish dynamical accessibility.
why: A numerically optimized topology may not be the state reached by an experiment.
key_works: Hudson et al. (2002), *Eliminating Islands in High-Pressure Free-Boundary Stellarator Magnetohydrodynamic Equilibrium Solutions*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.275003.

title: Certified relaxation gaps in coil optimization
open: Bound the difference between an optimized continuous-current representation and the best manufacturable discrete-coil realization, including cases where a global optimum is not certified.
status: QUADCOIL provides exact global solutions in some parameter regions and useful approximate solutions elsewhere; extracting certified physical-coil quality remains a distinct problem.
why: A favorable mathematical relaxation may conceal expensive discretization losses.
key_works: Fu et al. (2024–2025), *Global Stellarator Coil Optimization with Quadratic Constraints and Objectives*, arXiv:2408.08267.

title: Quantified flexibility of optimized stellarators
open: Optimize not just one plasma configuration but a sufficiently broad family reachable with permitted coil currents, while maintaining conductor-strain and engineering constraints.
status: CSX single-stage design incorporates engineering constraints and possible auxiliary coils; a general quantitative flexibility–performance tradeoff remains open.
why: An exceptionally optimized but inflexible machine may be difficult to commission or operate.
key_works: Baillod et al. (2024), *Integrating Novel Stellarator Single-Stage Optimization Algorithms to Design the Columbia Stellarator Experiment*, arXiv:2409.05261.

title: Experimental discrimination of hydrogen self-clustering
open: Distinguish hydrogen self-clustering in tungsten from trapping at pre-existing vacancies, dislocations, or impurities using experiments with independently characterized defect populations.
status: Density-functional and statistical models predict self-clustering mechanisms; their quantitative contribution under plasma exposure remains to be isolated.
why: Different nucleation mechanisms imply different retention and blister-prevention strategies.
key_works: Hou et al. (2017), *Hydrogen bubble nucleation by self-clustering: Density Functional Theory and statistical models studies using tungsten as a model system*, arXiv:1712.09606.

title: Self-passivation after preferential alloy erosion
open: Determine whether W–Cr–Y and related self-passivating alloys retain protective oxidation behavior after plasma exposure preferentially removes alloying elements.
status: Self-passivating tungsten alloys have demonstrated favorable oxidation behavior; the surface composition after service is a separate qualification variable.
why: Accident protection must work on the used component, not just a freshly manufactured specimen.
key_works: Calvo et al. (2018), *Self-passivating tungsten alloys of the system W-Cr-Y for high temperature applications*, DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrmhm.2018.01.018.

title: Direct validation of RF current condensation
open: Measure the predicted nonlinear localization of radio-frequency heating and current within a magnetic island, separating it from ordinary deposition changes.
status: RF current condensation was proposed in 2018, with later work developing validation strategies. The mechanism requires a discriminating experimental test.
why: It could reduce the power required to suppress dangerous tearing modes.
key_works: Reiman and Fisch (2018), *Suppression of Tearing Modes by Radio Frequency Current Condensation*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.225001; arXiv:1806.09260.

title: Robust O–X–B conversion in turbulent edges
open: Maintain efficient ordinary-to-extraordinary-to-Bernstein-wave conversion despite fluctuating density gradients, launch angle errors, and evolving edge geometry.
status: Electron-Bernstein-wave current drive was demonstrated in W7-AS in 2003; robust reactor-compatible coupling is the unresolved extension.
why: Bernstein waves can access overdense plasma only through a reliable coupling pathway.
key_works: Laqua et al. (2003), *Electron-Bernstein-Wave Current Drive in an Overdense Plasma at the Wendelstein 7-AS Stellarator*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.075003.

title: Three-ion heating under changing fuel composition
open: Maintain efficient three-ion cyclotron heating while fuel ratios, minority populations, and fast-ion distributions evolve.
status: Three-ion scenarios have substantial experimental and theoretical support; their efficiency depends sensitively on composition and resonant absorbers.
why: A narrow composition window could be difficult to preserve during reactor transients.
key_works: Kazakov et al. (2021), *Physics and applications of three-ion ICRF scenarios for fusion research*, *Physics of Plasmas* 28, 020501.

title: Composition-dependent pellet-plasmoid drift
open: Predict radial drift of the ablation cloud for mixed-material pellets, including ionization, radiation, magnetic perturbations, and changing electrical conductivity.
status: Three-dimensional MHD modeling published in 2024 advances drift prediction; reliable mixture-dependent assimilation remains a further challenge.
why: Pellet material can drift away from the region where it is needed.
key_works: Kong et al. (2024), *3D MHD modelling of plasmoid drift following massive material injection in a tokamak*, arXiv:2407.01399.

title: Predictive non-LTE hohlraum emission
open: Construct atomic-kinetics models that predict ignition-scale hohlraum spectra and drive without experiment-specific correction multipliers.
status: Improved non-LTE modeling was published in 2025; matching the full spectrum and target drive remains the relevant test.
why: An incorrect radiation spectrum can change both ablation and preheat.
key_works: Farmer et al. (2025), *Toward an improved nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium model for more predictive simulations of ignition scale hohlraums*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0267536.

title: Graded inner shells robust to fabrication uncertainty
open: Optimize double-shell material gradients against measured uncertainty in thickness, composition, surface finish, and assembly—not only nominal simulated yield.
status: Multifidelity optimization has identified promising graded-shell designs; robust experimental realization remains a further step.
why: A narrow numerical optimum may have poor manufacturing yield.
key_works: Vazirani et al. (2023), *Coupling multi-fidelity xRAGE with machine learning for graded inner shell design optimization in double shell capsules*, *Physics of Plasmas* 30, 062704.

title: Chirping criteria far from marginal stability
open: Extend chirping-versus-steady-frequency criteria to strongly driven modes with evolving backgrounds and significant redistribution of energetic particles.
status: Existing criteria incorporate collisions and turbulence and have experimental comparisons; near-threshold reasoning does not automatically cover strongly nonlinear bursts.
why: Different nonlinear mode behavior produces very different particle-loss risks.
key_works: Duarte et al. (2017), *Prediction of Nonlinear Evolution Character of Energetic-Particle-Driven Instabilities*, PPPL-5366.

title: Whistler wave-number and resonance identification
open: Measure the wave-vector distribution and damping of runaway-driven whistlers sufficiently well to determine which electron energies and pitch angles they actually scatter.
status: Detailed DIII-D characterization published in 2025 improves frequency and temporal constraints; frequency measurements alone do not uniquely identify resonance.
why: An observed wave may couple weakly to the electrons responsible for damage.
key_works: Choudhury et al. (2025), *Detailed characterization of runaway electron driven whistler waves in low-density DIII-D discharges*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0277589.
